assessment: A 36-card bench (34 distinct names: Vampire Nocturnus and Unholy Officiant each appear as two printings) that is mostly the parts bin an evolving typal deck should keep: outgrown tribe bodies, spares of maindeck cards (Strefan, Vito), one unplayable card (Runo Stromkirk, blue identity), plus three things that actually earn attention — a free sac outlet the Grave Pact/Voldaren Pariah maindeck conspicuously lacks, a second loss-on-gain half (Sanguine Bond) for the verified drain knockout, and a coherent aristocrats sub-package. With no pilot_feedback.md the posture is conservative: one promotion, two conditional swaps, and the rest stays in the box with reasons.

swaps.when: Unconditional — every game this 99 plays draws toward Grave Pact or Voldaren Pariah, and the maindeck role histogram has zero sac-outlet entries; this is the promote case, applied at the next revision rather than pod-by-pod
swaps.why: Viscera Seer is the deck's only route to killing its own creatures on demand: with Grave Pact it converts each free eminence token into an each-opponent edict at instant speed, and it is the card that makes Voldaren Pariah's 'sacrifice three other creatures' flip castable — while Vampire Interloper is a 2/1 flyer that can't block and carries no other text; both are one-mana Vampire casts, so the eminence token is a wash.

citations.quote: cut duplicated function before any uncovered class, and cut the ceiling card before the median one

swaps.when: Once your pod has seen the Vito loop (stacks 001/004) and starts holding creature removal for the drain half — Bond is the redundant copy that lives where Swords to Plowshares can't reach
swaps.why: Sanguine Bond's trigger is word-for-word Vito's first ability ('Whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life'), so it pairs with maindeck Exquisite Blood — the famous two-enchantment infinite — and with Bloodthirsty Conqueror, the same loop shape stacks 001 and 004 verified for Vito, on an enchantment instead of a 3-toughness creature; the Bond pairings themselves are unverified (see opens_lines). Stensia Masquerade is the narrowest maindeck buff: attacker-only first strike the deck already gets from Stromkirk Captain, plus slow one-at-a-time counters that Edgar's attack trigger outclasses.

citations.quote: consistency has two purchases: redundancy (more cards doing the job) or tutoring (cards that fetch it)

swaps.when: Pods leaning on graveyard recursion or opposing death-trigger engines (reanimator, aristocrats seats) — a meta call, not a default
swaps.why: With maindeck Grave Pact, every eminence-token death forces each opponent to sacrifice a creature — and Kalitas's replacement exiles each nontoken creature that would die that way (no reanimation, no death triggers for them) while handing you a 2/2 Zombie per exile; Vampire Nighthawk is duplicated function next to Nighthawk Scavenger, the same three-mana flying/deathtouch/lifelink body the deck already runs in its power-crept form.

citations.quote: Depth is a meta call: copy the answer your table beats you with.
cut duplicated function before any uncovered class

opens_lines.why_plausible: Bond duplicates Vito's loss-on-gain trigger verbatim, and stack 001 verified Exquisite Blood + Vito as a deterministic table-kill from any life exchange; Bond + Exquisite is the classic two-enchantment version of the same shape, and strategic_frame.candidate_missing_lines already flags it as sideboard-conditional — but no artifact covers the Bond pairing, and 001 verifies the Vito loop, not this one

Mirrors the Conqueror + Vito loop that stack 004 verified, with Bond supplying the loss-on-gain half from an enchantment; sideboard-facts counts it among the 2 lines Bond completes that the deck cannot currently assemble — unverified until a checker-passed artifact exists for this exact pair

long_term_defaults.why: The maindeck has zero sac-outlet roles next to Grave Pact and Voldaren Pariah; a free, instant-speed outlet on a one-mana Vampire body is better than Vampire Interloper in every pod this deck sits down at — see the first swap
Conditional redundancy: five mana that does nothing without a gain engine already online; it comes in when the pod answers Vito on sight, not by default
A meta answer to recursion and death-trigger decks that happens to combo with Grave Pact edicts; in a vacuum it is a slower body than the maindeck three-drops

The strongest artifact on the bench — cost reduction on ~40 Vampire casts plus a free upkeep impulse, and it turns Forerunner of the Legion's tutor-to-top into tutor-to-hand — but the deck already runs Vanquisher's Banner and Bontu's Monument in the same slot class; first-in if the pilot ever asks for more velocity

Two damage to each opponent per eminence token is real non-combat reach against ~120 combined life, but it is a non-Vampire (no eminence trigger, no lord support) in a deck with only 9 red cards and 22 red source targets; a deliberate power-up, not a default
Grows off every token death and refunds a lifelinker board when she dies — decent wrath insurance — but the deck's rebuild plan is already eminence itself, which costs zero slots

long_term_defaults.card: Sorin of House Markov // Sorin, Ravenous Neonate
long_term_defaults.why: A two-mana lifelink Vampire whose extort feeds Vito-style triggers, but the flip condition (gain 3+ in a turn, postcombat) is win-more here and the planeswalker face does not advance the go-wide plan

+2/+1 and flying tribe-wide when the top card is black is a real lord, but {1}{B}{B}{B} is the heaviest pip cost in the tribe and the trigger whiffs on the deck's 34 lands and white/red spells; the PDP13 promo copy is a spare of the M13 copy either way
Spare copy — Strefan is already in the maindeck; this one exists to replace a lost or worn card, not to be swapped in

long_term_defaults.card: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
long_term_defaults.why: Spare copy of the maindeck loop piece that stacks 001 and 004 verified; keep it sleeved nearby precisely because the maindeck copy is the most removal-magnetic card in the 99, but a second copy cannot be swapped in next to the first
A flexible ETB Vampire (Pest, draw, or graveyard exile) with no maindeck slot weaker than it; the graveyard-exile mode is why it stays in the box as meta insurance
One Blood token and gain-1-per-Blood-sacrifice is Strefan support, but Strefan is the only maindeck Blood producer — the package is too thin to pay off a vanilla 1/4
A one-mana vigilance body with a five-mana pump; the deck's one-drop slots are already better (Knight of the Ebon Legion, Vampire of the Dire Moon); the second VOW printing is a spare of the first

long_term_defaults.card: Runo Stromkirk // Krothuss, Lord of the Deep
long_term_defaults.why: Outside Edgar's Mardu colour identity ({1}{U}{B}) — unplayable in this deck, per the sideboard-facts flag; it lives here as a collection card, nothing more
A three-mana 3/2 trampler making Blood on connect is below the maindeck three-drop bar (Sanctum Seeker, Captivating Vampire) and the Blood package is one card deep
A two-mana 2/1 that first-strikes on the attack and leaves one Blood behind; strictly filler next to the maindeck two-drop lords and utility bodies

The best pure draw engine on the bench — the deck gains life incidentally almost every turn (lifelink bodies, drains, Ocelot Pride), so the end-step pay-{2}-draw is near-reliable; the deck's draw:engine count is only 2, making Purifier the second-in after Herald's Horn if consistency ever feels short
'Attack with exactly two creatures' is anti-synergy with a go-wide token deck whose plan is seven-Vampire alpha strikes (stack 003's scenario); wrong list for this card
A five-mana payoff that needs a Blood token per attack in a deck whose only maindeck Blood source is Strefan's end step; too slow and too conditional
A two-mana 1/1 flyer whose value is a four-mana graveyard exhale for two Bats; no synergy hook here — the Bats are not Vampires and never trigger eminence

Each-opponent life loss off tapped attackers stacks with Exquisite Blood and Bloodthirsty Conqueror's gain-on-loss triggers, and it survives sweepers — a genuinely interesting reach card, but colourless artifact slots are contested (Vanquisher's Banner, Akroma's Memorial) and no feedback asks for more reach
A two-mana vigilant taxer that either taps opposing rocks/creatures on entry or hands you lifelinker Vampire tokens — the best fair two-drop on the bench, waiting on a two-drop slot to open

A one-mana Vampire that sacrifices another creature for {B}{B}{B} restricted to Vampire/Cleric/Demon spells — a real ritual-dork and third sac outlet if the aristocrats package is ever adopted wholesale, but not ahead of Viscera Seer on any axis this deck cares about
A convoke lord with madness is fine lord-redundancy behind Legion Lieutenant, Captivating Vampire, and Stromkirk Captain, but the deck is not short on anthems — it is short on sac outlets and draw
One-shot intimidate on a single creature per black ETB is weaker evasion than the maindeck's Cover of Darkness, which does the job tribe-wide

A repeatable Exsanguinate is tempting with two gain-on-loss enchantments in the maindeck, but the prepare condition routes through single-target combat damage — slow and fragile next to the drains the deck already runs
This is what a sideboard card looks like by design: two-mana graveyard hate with a body, in for graveyard pods, out otherwise; it stays benched until the meta asks
Sac outlet number two, and the only one that pays in tribe-wide +1/+1 counters (which Edgar's attack trigger then compounds); the natural second-in if the Viscera Seer promotion proves out

The aristocrats payoff: each token death drains 1 and gains 1 — and every gain is a Vito/Sanguine Bond trigger — but without an adopted sac outlet the deaths are not on demand, so the payoff waits on the package
Attack-triggered sacrifice-for-a-card is a fourth outlet plus draw, but it only fires once per combat and telegraphs; package depth, not a starter

Tutor-to-top for any Vampire (including Bloodthirsty Conqueror, half of the 004-verified loop) is real, but it costs a turn of draw unless Herald's Horn is also in play to lift the card at upkeep — a pairing worth remembering if the pilot ever asks for both

long_term_defaults.card: Aclazotz, Deepest Betrayal // Temple of the Dead
long_term_defaults.why: A self-recurring five-drop that punishes each opponent per attack and comes back as a land — arguably the best top-end card on the bench in a curve with only two spells above five, but cutting a maindeck card for a five-drop needs pilot appetite this analysis does not have

A repeatable Sign in Blood behind a trivially-met gain-2 condition is the third-best draw option benched (after Herald's Horn and Markov Purifier); worth a look the day the pilot reports running out of gas

A non-Vampire Human that triggers neither eminence nor any lord; the +1/+1-counter flying payoff reads well against the deck's 9 buff:counters roles but the counters arrive too sporadically (Edgar attack, Drana) to build around

gaps: No pilot_feedback.md exists for this deck — appetite unknown, so this analysis defaults to the conservative posture (one promotion, two conditional swaps); a feedback file stating target bracket or desired aggression would change the swap budget

No manual_prose.json for this deck, and issue.json contains no sideboard prose — there is no published sideboard stance to align with or contradict; the first published mention of these cards will be whatever merges from this analysis

The strategy corpus has no aristocrats/sacrifice-value section (strategic_frame.gaps confirms: 'aristocrats sacrifice drain' tops out at 0.19 on politics) — the Viscera Seer promotion and the package reads on Cruel Celebrant / Indulgent Aristocrat / Master of Dark Rites rest on oracle-text interactions alone; a research-strategy pass on aristocrats theory would ground them
No typal/lord-density section in the corpus — the lord-vs-body calls on Vampire Nocturnus and Markov Baron are uncited for the same reason

Sanguine Bond + Exquisite Blood and Sanguine Bond + Bloodthirsty Conqueror are unverified — a /resolve-stack run on either pair would settle whether the Bond swap carries the same verified table-kill as stacks 001/004, and stack 001's scenario is a ready template
sideboard-facts reports no EDHREC rank for any bench card, so every 'stronger default' claim here argues from the deck's needs, never from popularity
